itens.t: Israel Election Results: No Clear Winner Projected, Deadlocked Parliament Set for Coalitions

itens.t: Study Reveals How the 'Bad Apple Effect' Rapidly Spreads Through Groups
itens.r: New scientific research published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B has overturned the notion that humans make decisions entirely independently. The study demonstrates how unethical behavior quickly cascades through a group via the 'bad apple effect'.
itens.d:
A scientific study published in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B has explored the 'bad apple effect' in groups. Led by Lucas Molleman of the University of Amsterdam, the research involved 750 participants in the United States making choices in an online test.

The findings show that witnessing rule violations by others can encourage observers to commit even greater infractions. This behavior is especially pronounced when the transgressions are severe and come from individuals who share political affinities.
